labels.text: Picks the best model for each message

S79.01.needs: a paid account (Free accounts see "Auto (free) · community models, capacity varies" instead)
S79.01.note: Auto row is shown only on paid plans; the choice is visible only as the answer's model, no per-answer model name was found.
steps: Sign in with a paid account.
Click the model name button at the bottom of the message box (its accessible name ends in "Change model").
Find the row labelled "Auto" with the text "Picks the best model for each message" and click it.
Send a short message and an image-free question, then look at the answer: it should come from a model chosen by Auto, not a fixed one.
S79.01.where: Composer model button (the selected model name, e.g. under the message box) > top row "Auto"

S79.02.note: Model names are read from the catalogue at runtime, so no fixed model name is written in the code.
steps: Sign in with a paid account.
Click the model name button at the bottom of the message box.
Click any model row other than "Auto", for example one listed under "Recommended".
Send a message and check that the model name shown in the composer button is the one you picked.
S79.02.where: Composer model button > model rows below "Auto" (under "Recommended" or the model list)

labels.text: No default, use the model you last picked

S79.03.note: The exact name of the settings item in the More menu was not confirmed in the code.
steps: Open Projects from the left sidebar and open a project.
Click the More (···) button at the top of the project and open its settings.
Find the "Default model" field and pick a model from the dropdown.
Save, open a new chat in that project and check the composer shows the chosen model.
S79.03.where: Projects > open a project > the More (···) button > project settings, then the "Default model" field

S79.04.note: No visible row mentions coding or reasoning; the Expected example (premium for coding) is not stated on screen.
steps: Sign in with a paid account.
Click the model name button at the bottom of the message box.
Click "Instant", "Best" or "Economy" under the "Auto" row.
Send a question about coding or reasoning and compare the answer's model with what the row said.
S79.04.where: Composer model button > "Auto" row, then the profile rows "Instant", "Best", "Economy" below it

labels.text: Answers fastest, on the quickest models your plan includes.

steps: Sign in with a paid account.
Click the model name button at the bottom of the message box.
Click the row "Instant" with the text "Answers fastest, on the quickest models your plan includes."
Send a short question and check the answer arrives quickly and the composer shows a fast model.

labels.text: The most capable model your plan includes, for harder work.

steps: Sign in with a paid account.
Click the model name button at the bottom of the message box.
Click the row "Best" with the text "The most capable model your plan includes, for harder work."
Send a hard question and check the composer shows the most capable model for your plan.

labels.text: The lowest-cost model that can handle the task.

steps: Sign in with a paid account.
Click the model name button at the bottom of the message box.
Click the row "Economy" with the text "The lowest-cost model that can handle the task."
Send a simple question and check the composer shows a low-cost model.

S79.08.note: The Settings menu item that opens this section was not confirmed; there is no visible privacy-first routing profile, only this policy toggle.
steps: Open Settings and go to Workspace policy (organization admin access is needed to change it).
Find the row "Zero data retention only".
Turn on the toggle and save.
Send a request and check that it is refused rather than sent to a provider without zero data retention.
S79.08.where: Settings > Workspace policy > "Zero data retention only"

S79.09.note: Intent classification is internal routing logic in packages/ai/routing/src/classify.ts with no control of its own; its effect shows only as the model chosen.

S79.10.note: Tool needs are classified on the server (request-processor.ts) with no control of its own.

S79.11.note: Attached-media routing is internal; the only visible result is the "Choose a compatible model" offer (see S79.21).

S79.12.note: Complexity classification is internal (packages/ai/routing/src/task-family.ts) with no visible control.

S79.13.note: Freshness detection is server-side with no visible control; the effect shows only in the answer.

S79.14.note: Candidate filtering is a server rule; its effect is visible only as which models appear in the picker.

S79.15.note: Provider route choice is server-side ranking with no control of its own.

S79.16.note: A server rule. Visible sign: a model picked by hand is not replaced; the "Moved to" line (S79.26) appears only for Auto moves.

S79.19.note: Quota-aware routing is server-side with no control of its own.

S79.20.note: Health fallback is server-side. A visible fallback notice exists (role=status, testid fallback-reason-notice in MessageBubble.tsx) but its wording was not read.

S79.21.needs: a file to upload, a model that cannot read it
S79.21.note: This is an offer to switch on a conflict; a switch offer for a better answer (not for attachments) was not found.
steps: Select a model that cannot read images.
Attach an image to the message box.
Read the warning and click "Choose a compatible model".
Pick a model from the list and check the composer switches to it and the attachment is kept.
S79.21.where: Message box > attach a file or image that the selected model cannot read > "Choose a compatible model"

labels.text: Ask every model the same thing

S79.24.needs: a paid account (at least two models your plan includes)
S79.24.note: The button that opens the compare page was not confirmed; the scale icon has no visible text.
steps: Open the models catalogue.
Click the scale icon on two models (its accessible name is "Compare <model name>").
Open the compare answers view and type one prompt in the box "Ask every model the same thing".
Press send and check each model returns its own answer side by side.
S79.24.where: Models (catalogue) > the Compare button (scale icon) on two or more model cards > Compare answers page

labels.text: the model this chat was already using

S79.26.needs: a paid account, a long chat or a case where Auto moves
S79.26.note: The line appears only after an Auto move, so a tester cannot force it.
steps: Start a chat with Auto and keep sending messages until Auto moves to another model (it is not forced).
Look at the answer where the model changed.
Read the line under the answer that starts with "Moved to".
Check the reason text matches the reasons listed in the contracts file.
S79.26.where: A chat answer > the small line "Moved to <model>: <reason>" under the answer (appears only when Auto switched models)

S79.27.note: Only the "Moved to" receipt (apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/MessageBubble.tsx) was found, and it shows only after a move; no per-answer model name was found.

S79.28.note: Searched apps/web and packages/ui for routing policy version text: none found; trace code is in packages/ai/routing/src/routing-trace.ts and a service in apps/web/lib/services/model-rollout/.

S79.30.note: Fallback on ambiguous classification is server-side; the visible result is a normal answer.
